stories.headline: What does a fair fantasy hockey trade offer for Connor McDavid look like?
stories.summary: What would a fair trade offer for the highest-scoring player in fantasy hockey look like? Here are five tips.
stories.body:
"McDavid's controlling every single game he's playing right now. He's on a whole different level than anyone else in the League right now."

- Panthers forward Matthew Tkachuk, following Edmonton's 5-2 win over Florida

Reflecting back to preseason fantasy discussions, it's almost adorable how earnestly and robustly many of us debated which skater should be selected first overall. Even more delightfully cute, mind you, for fantasy managers who happened to acquire Connor McDavid either through a cunning sense of insight, or because a manager with a higher draft pick instead selected Nathan MacKinnon, Nikita Kucherov, Macklin Celebrini or other. Remember, McDavid was projected to take a minor step back in the production department under Mike Babcock's fresh defense-first system. Right. Now we're keeping daily track of where the league's top producer -- a ridiculous 55 points in 23 games thus far -- is pacing out relative to Wayne Gretzky's 215 points earned 1985-86. For hockey fans everywhere, this is a treat to experience.

Which also, getting back to our specific intents and purposes, inspires the question: What's McDavid's fantasy trade value now? Everyone has a price, including the league's list-of-one ultra-megastar. So, after scanning some public trade boards for what the elite center is actually commanding in return -- in some cases way too much and others not early enough -- I threw out the query to fellow managers across the continent, including those in my Fantasy Sports & Gaming Association Champions League. My confidential straw poll was focused on fantasy redraft competition (we can open up the conversation to include keeper leagues at a later date) drew a rather consistent response.

What would a Conor McDavid trade even look like?
"You'd have to be convinced you'd have an opportunity to win the league off of a trade like that. I'd need three top-15 players. Kirill Kaprizov, Macklin Celebrini and Evan Bouchard? And I'd probably have to be in a situation where I was bumping some non-contributors from my roster with those players."

"In a 12 team redraft league, I'd want one of Leon Draisaitl, Nikita Kucherov, Celebrini, or Nathan MacKinnon (once healthy) plus another significant piece. For instance, Kucherov plus Bouchard or Draisaitl plus Eichel. I'd consider McDavid pretty much untouchable, so the offer would need to be a haul. Wouldn't want a goalie, they're too volatile."

"Because it is fantasy hockey, any trade is possible. It truly depends on the league and format. I did see McDavid go for something crazy like Jesper Wallstedt, Leon Draisaitl, and Adam Fox recently."

"I'm not giving him away for anything. My league is too small. So is my roster. He carries too much weight."

The last point is critical. In shallow leagues with precious few lineup spots, it's difficult to justify moving such a fantasy outlier -- one capable of singularly seizing weekly victory in head-to-head competition -- for anything less than two other exceptional skaters.

It makes little sense to jettison the only NHLer who's averaging more than 4.0 fantasy points/game, along with being forced to move another reasonably valuable performer, say David Pastrnak or Beckett Sennecke, to accommodate a top-tier individual and player near equal in value to a Pastrnak or Sennecke etc. Right? The fantasy math doesn't make sense. Especially when considering McDavid posts the most legit potential to go off any night of the week. So this is only worth examining in deeper leagues where, as touched on above, a two-or-more-for-one-deal involves dropping so-called non-contributors to make room for other valued performers.

Is a McDavid trade even a serious consideration?
As you can see in this chart of the most involved players in trade discussions, approved trades for McDavid are rare. In fact, McDavid has been the target of the most trade offers (i.e. the team offering wants to get him back), but at 6.2%, he has the lowest acceptance rate of any of the 267 players with a minimum of 1,000 trade offers.

Kucherov, the most-traded player, has seen 11.3% of trade offers in which he was involved accepted. Andrei Vasilevskiy has been the most-traded goalie in the past 30 days and the overall "accepted" leader at 14.6%)

I once again harassed my fellow managers on who they would actually move to acquire the best player on the planet. Turns out there's little appetite to relinquish Draisaitl or Bouchard as part of a package, which makes sense since both exceptional players also benefit every game from battling alongside McDavid. In fact, thanks to his goal-scoring prowess, Draisaitl is averaging more fantasy points per game than his running mate these past three weeks. Bouchard is the only 3.0-plus point defender in ESPN standard leagues. On the other hand, most agreed Kucherov, MacKinnon (when healthy), Celebrini, and others might be worth surrendering, depending on who else needed to be included in the deal.

Is trading away Conor McDavid the right move for you?

Okay, so after polling several esteemed members of the fantasy hockey community, perusing online trade market boards, and crunching some numbers, I'm offering the following list of boxes to check when considering dealing away Edmonton's No. 97. Take note, this entire exercise falls under the necessary assumption that McDavid remains healthy for the majority of the season, and, as in real life, maintains the fair spirit of both managers benefiting from the deal.

Your league comprises at least 150 total skaters and McDavid takes up less than approximately 5% of your lineup when active. That means a 10-team league starting 15 forwards and 5 defensemen, but the deeper, the better. Otherwise, unless your trading partner is relinquishing more than one exceptional performer, you're not getting back fair value in exchange for giving up another otherwise valuable contributor.
The math adds up, obviously. For instance, in a two-for-one -- which I'd stick with unless your league is exceptionally large and/or you sport several substantial roster flaws -- at least one regular skater averaging more than 3.0 points and another around the 2.7 range. Otherwise, the math doesn't math for such a singular fantasy powerhouse.
You're satisfying a positional weakness. Stacked up front but your fantasy blue line stinks? Assuming Bouchard isn't part of the discussion, how about Matthew Schaefer or similar along with a top-10 forward? A league peer with a more balanced lineup should be willing to broker such an arrangement.
You're in deep goaltending doo-doo. While I don't disagree that goalies are often volatile, you're also not winning anything with a really vulnerable crease. Without question, there are managers out there who drafted Sergei Bobrovsky, Scott Wedgewood or Igor Shesterkin (IR) who are now facing a long, miserable season unless, of course they acquire a net-minding heavyweight, plus more, in exchange for the Oilers captain.
You feel McDavid's current 2.4 point/game run is substantially unsustainable. Hardly an unreasonable hunch considering he's still a human being and, as we've been reminded recently by the man himself, not a robot. A quarter into the season, other teams are undoubtedly going to increase their focus on muffling the guy.

Let's leave it there. Whether you're looking to move McDavid, acquire him, or enjoying the superstar's quest to make more history, we're all unquestionably in for one of the greatest individual campaigns in NHL history.

stories.headline: Pete Rose posthumously pardoned by President Donald Trump
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said he has posthumously pardoned Pete Rose more than two years after the baseball star's death and a year after he was reinstated by MLB.
stories.body:
WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump on Thursday said he had posthumously pardoned Pete Rose more than two years after the baseball star's death and a year after he was reinstated by Major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred.

"I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND," Trump posted on social media.

Rose, baseball's career hits leader at 4,256, entered guilty pleas on April 20, 1990, to two counts of filing false tax returns, admitting he failed to report $354,968 during a four-year period. That was about eight months after Rose agreed to a permanent ban from baseball.

"I know I'm not a bad person, but I did make some mistakes and it's in the eyes of the judge," Rose said that night during his weekly talk show on WCKY-AM in Cincinnati. "All you can say is it's up to the judge."

The pardon comes after Manfred issued a sweeping decision last May that opened a pathway for Rose to be considered for baseball's Hall of Fame. Manfred declared that individuals on MLB's permanently ineligible list would have their statuses restored at death, a ruling that impacted 17 people, most notably Rose and Shoeless Joe Jackson.

Under a rule adopted by the Hall's board of directors in 1991, anyone on the permanently ineligible list can't be considered for election to the Hall. The earliest Rose or Jackson could now be inducted would be in 2028.

Rose agreed to his permanent ban in August 1989 after Major League Baseball investigator John M. Dowd concluded he bet numerous times on the Cincinnati Reds while playing on and managing his hometown team from 1985 to 1987.

Facing a sentence of up to six years in prison and $500,000 in fines, Rose was sentenced on July 19, 1990, by U.S. District Judge S. Arthur Spiegel in Cincinnati to five months in prison. He also was fined $50,000 and ordered to perform 1,000 hours of community service as a gym teacher's assistant with inner-city youths in Cincinnati as part of a one-year probation period. The first three months of the probation were to be spent at the halfway house.

Rose repaid $366,042 to the Internal Revenue Service.

"History and the tincture of time will decide his place among the all-time greats of baseball," Spiegel said. "With regard to Pete Rose, the individual, he has broken the law, admitted his guilt, and stands ready to pay the penalty. Under our system of law and sense of fairness, when he has completed his sentence, he will have paid his debt to society and should be accepted by society as rehabilitated. Only time will tell whether he is to be restored to his position of honor for his accomplishment on the ball fields of America."

Rose reported that Aug. 10 to the U.S. Penitentiary Marion Camp in Illinois, a minimum-security facility, and was released Jan. 7, 1991. He entered Talbert House to start serving his probation and departed on April 5.

A 17-time All-Star during a playing career from 1963 to 1986, Rose was the 1963 National League Rookie of the Year, 1973 MVP and 1975 World Series MVP. A three-time NL batting champion, he broke the prior hits record of 4,191 set by Ty Cobb from 1905 to 1928.

stories.headline: 2027 NFL draft Big Board rankings: Mel Kiper's top 25 prospects, best by position
stories.summary: Six quarterbacks and six receivers ranked in the top 25? Mel Kiper Jr. stacks the best players on the 2027 draft board as of mid-November.
stories.body:
I'm getting excited for the 2027 NFL draft. And as we get closer and closer to the end of the 2026 college football regular season, and I'm updating my Big Board once again.

My normal disclaimer: This is not a mock draft. What follows isn't any form of prediction for when or where players will get picked once we hit Round 1 on April 29 in Washington D.C. Instead, this is simply my personal ranking of the best players in the class. The list below is based on my own evaluations from what I see on film and some conversations I've had around the NFL. And remember that a lot can change here. Players will rise and fall on the board, and some will even return to school for another year at the collegiate level before turning pro in the future.

Here is my current ranking of the top 25 prospects in the 2027 draft class. And at the bottom, I've included the best players at each position. Check back regularly right through draft day -- I will keep this list updated as the class continues to take shape. But one spot that might not change at all is No. 1 ...

Jump to:

Positional rankings

1. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State
Height: 6-foot-4 | Weight: 222 pounds | Previous rank: 1

2026 stats over 10 games: 80 catches, 1,317 receiving yards, 15 touchdown catches

Smith is very clearly the best player in this draft class. He's big, fast and physical, and he snatches the ball on the run cleanly. On 329 career targets, he has just seven drops. And Smith has the body control to make tough catches. I love the way that he is always looking to improve, too. Smith worked on his after-the-catch skills heading into the 2026 season, and he has been able to make some things happen with the ball in his hands using his strength and speed.

Ohio State continues to feed him targets (well north of 10 per game), and nobody can cover him. That was very apparent against Illinois in September, when he caught 12 balls for 217 yards and four touchdowns. In three seasons at Ohio State, he has 42 career touchdown catches, and he's averaging 15.9 yards per catch. Just an incredible football player.

2. Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 215 | Previous rank: 2

2026 stats over 10 games: 66.4% completion rate, 3,239 passing yards, 30 touchdown passes, 10 interceptions; 244 rushing yards, four rushing touchdowns

Mestemaker didn't even start at quarterback for his high school team; he was the punter, played some safety and was the backup QB. Then he walked on at North Texas in 2024 as a QB before becoming the starter in 2025. After throwing for more than 4,000 yards, Mestemaker transferred with coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State. It's an incredible story.

His toolbox is also pretty incredible. I love the way he scans the field and bides his time in the pocket. Mestemaker has the big arm to make all of the throws, with 51 completions going for 20-plus yards this season (most in the FBS). But he also has the mobility to pick up nice chunks of yardage on the ground. Mestemaker shows linebacker-esque toughness and plays with a competitive edge. He doesn't turn 21 years old until January, so there's a lot of untapped potential.

3. Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 197 | Previous rank: 3

2026 stats over eight games: 18 tackles, five pass breakups, one forced fumble

Moore is exactly what NFL coaches look for in a lockdown cornerback. He has elite length and ball skills, with seven interceptions and 23 pass breakups over his three-year career. He's scheme versatile, too. Moore displays great awareness and instincts in coverage, and he's a silky smooth mover. His footwork is truly outstanding. Moore consistently performs at a high level, but he's still looking for his first pick of the season.

4. CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 215 | Previous rank: 4

2026 stats over 10 games: 67.9% completion rate, 2,385 passing yards, 23 touchdown passes, two interceptions; 100 rushing yards, three rushing touchdowns

There's a lot to like in Carr's game. He's smart and processes quickly before and after the snap, which is part of the reason he has taken just three sacks all season. He's accurate to all levels and throws with anticipation. And while his arm strength is good but not great, he can cause conflict for defenses with his mobility. Carr can throw on the move or pick up a first down on the ground. Nothing fazes him, and he's always in control. In short, Carr is pretty advanced in the key areas of NFL-level quarterback play. And he was outstanding in Notre Dame's biggest game of the season, throwing for 319 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions against Miami.

5. Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 246 | Previous rank: 5

2026 stats over eight games: 32 tackles, 10.5 sacks, 16.0 tackles for loss, 25 pressures, two forced fumbles, eight run stops

Did you catch Simmons against Tennessee in September? He had 5.5 sacks in that game alone. The production is off the charts -- he has 31.5 sacks, 44.5 tackles for loss and eight forced fumbles over three seasons. Simmons -- who has missed some time with an ankle injury -- is the type of closer most NFL defenses want rushing off the edge. He is explosive out of the blocks with natural bend, and he can beat opponents with outside or inside moves. And he isn't given enough credit for the power element in his game.

6. Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana
Height: 6-4 | Weight: 208 | Previous rank: 9

2026 stats over 10 games: 53 catches, 950 receiving yards, 10 touchdown catches

I love the way Becker attacks the football. He consistently wins in tight coverage with his big frame, excellent hands and nice adjustments to find the ball in the air. Becker can locate the open spots in the coverage, and he can stretch the field with his speed. He has averaged 17.9 yards per reception this season. I'll be watching him at the combine; he is going to test really well and should post a pretty fast 40-yard dash time.

7. Darian Mensah, QB, Miami (Fla.)
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 205 | Previous rank: 7

2026 stats over 10 games: 76.3% completion rate, 3,076 passing yards, 29 touchdown passes, 2 interceptions; 208 rushing yards, two rushing touchdowns

Mensah is at his third program in three years, transferring from Tulane to Duke (where he had 34 touchdown passes last season) and then on to Miami. To date, he has started 37 college games -- great experience for a kid who doesn't even turn 22 until January. He is a smooth, fluid passer with solid accuracy. He's smart in the pocket and manages the game really well. And the mobility is there for him to beat a defense as a rusher when the situation calls for it. Mensah currently leads the nation in completion percentage (76.3%) and QBR (88.6), and he's fourth in yards per attempt (9.7).

8. Chris Cole, LB, Georgia
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 235 | Previous rank: 8

2026 stats over 10 games: 63 tackles, 5.0 sacks, 12.0 tackles for loss, 22 pressures, 11 run stops, three pass breakups, two touchdowns

Cole is all over the field every Saturday. He's 235 pounds but looks like a safety at the second level. Cole is quick to diagnose thanks to his football IQ and then flies to the ball, especially in lateral pursuit. He is going to be a combine standout with that tremendous speed.

He is versatile, too. Cole can line up off the ball on the inside or on the outside, and he will consistently make plays against the run, in coverage and as an occasional pass rusher -- I see solid bend and burst off the edge. Cole is an outstanding player and is perfect for the way NFL football is played today.

9. Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 205 | Previous rank: 6

2026 stats over 10 games: 42 tackles, two interceptions, 12 pass breakups, 3.0 tackles for loss, four run stops

Hampton's confidence shows in his play. You can tell he loves matching up with the opposition's No. 1 receiver and going to battle. And more often than not, Hampton wins. He has allowed just 2.7 yards per pass attempt in his direction this season, which ranks fourth in the nation.

He plays an aggressive style, crowding receivers at the line of scrimmage, getting in his hip pocket and disrupting routes right away. Hampton can plant and drive on the ball (though his ball production is only moderate, with five career picks), and he has the recovery speed to make plays with his back to the QB when necessary.

10. Xavier Gilliam, DT, Tennessee
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 305 | Previous rank: 10

2026 stats over 10 games: 26 tackles, 6.0 sacks, 10.5 tackles for loss, 29 pressures, 10 run stops, two forced fumbles, three pass breakups

No player in college football has improved his draft stock more since the start of the season than Gilliam, starting with a three-sack outing against Furman to begin the campaign. He has been terrific in his first season with the Vols after following defensive coordinator Jim Knowles and transferring from Penn State. He is incredibly quick and explosive at the snap, and he generates a ton of interior pressure as a result. For a defensive tackle to go early in the draft, he must be consistently disruptive. Gilliam checks that box.

11. Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina
Height: 6-5 | Weight: 250 | Previous rank: 11

2026 stats over seven games: 16 tackles, 2.0 sacks, 5.0 tackles for loss, 18 pressures, three forced fumbles, four run stops

Stewart didn't play much in the early part of the season. He missed the first two games as he recovered from a back injury, and then he was suspended for one game for punching an Alabama player in the helmet and arguing with coaches on the sideline. But when he is playing, you can tell pretty quickly. His traits jump off the tape. It's just a matter of whether the production can catch up; Stewart has 13 career sacks over three seasons despite recording 86 pressures over those 31 games.

Stewart can vary his path to the QB, and he closes quickly with speed to power. He also has the big frame to hold the point and shed blockers against the run. The pass-rush ability is there, but he needs to figure out how to translate his physical traits into stat-sheet production on a more consistent basis.

12. Trevor Lauck, OT, Iowa
Height: 6-5 | Weight: 314 | Previous rank: 13

2026 stats over 10 games: 10 starts, zero sacks allowed, five pressures allowed

Lauck has been a mainstay at left tackle since the beginning of last season, starting 23 games there over that time (one sack allowed in 2025, none this season). His pass protection traits have stood out in particular this season, as he's technically sound. I see good footwork and balance on the tape, and he sustains well and finishes his blocks.

13. Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU
Height: 6-5 | Weight: 307 | Previous rank: 14

2026 stats over 10 games: 10 starts, one sack allowed, four pressures allowed

Seaton has started 32 games at left tackle, including 22 at Colorado before transferring to LSU before the 2026 season. He can push blockers past the QB and has improved as a run blocker, showing the ability to pull there. Seaton is in great shape this season, and he looks the part. He just needs to be coached up a little to realize his full potential as an elite left tackle.

14. Greg Johnson, G/C, Minnesota
Height: 6-6 | Weight: 325 | Previous rank: 16

2026 stats over 10 games: 10 starts, zero sacks allowed, one pressure allowed

Johnson has played significant snaps at left guard and center this season, and he's a high-level blocker at both spots. Versatility is one of his best traits; he had 50-plus snaps at both tackle spots last season in addition to his work on the interior. Johnson is a strong run blocker, with an aggressive, nasty edge to his game. He's powerful and can sustain well. But he also anchors well in pass protection, and he has never allowed a sack across 47 career games (38 starts).

15. Kade Pieper, G, Iowa
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 298 | Previous rank: 18

2026 stats over 10 games: 10 starts, zero sacks allowed, two pressures allowed

Pieper has played primarily right guard, but he's versatile, and some scouts might see him as a center in the pros. He's an athletic blocker who can pull and get to the second level to help spring big runs. He's also effective driving defenders off the ball. Over 36 career games (23 starts), Pieper has not allowed any sacks.

16. A.J. Holmes Jr., DT, Texas Tech
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 300 | Previous rank: NR

2026 stats over 10 games: 35 tackles, 8.0 sacks, 9.0 tackles for loss, 44 pressures, four run stops, one forced fumble

Holmes simply disrupts on the inside. He's powerful and quick, and his explosion has led to a 16.4% pressure rate in 2026. Holmes was solid with Houston in 2023 and 2024, and he had 4.5 sacks with the Red Raiders in 2025 after transferring, but he has hit another level this season. With cat-like reflexes, he gets in the backfield regularly and makes plays down the line of scrimmage. He commands double-teams but still manages to make an impact. And Holmes even has the versatility to play a little 3-4 end -- but I'd be keeping him inside where he dominates.

17. Nick Marsh, WR, Indiana
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 210 | Previous rank: 12

2026 stats over 10 games: 42 catches, 749 receiving yards, eight touchdown catches

The Michigan State transfer mixes physicality with athleticism. He has speed, and we see that in after-the-catch opportunities. But he also makes tough tight-window catches and fights for the ball. Marsh has improved there this season, winning in tight coverage more and more (12 contested catches). He has sure hands and can haul in off-target passes. Marsh just turned 20 years old, and the arrow is pointing up.

18. Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 315 | Previous rank: 15

2026 stats over 10 games: 25 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 5.5 tackles for loss, 20 pressures, seven run stops, four pass breakups

NFL teams love penetrating, disruptive interior defensive linemen, and Echoles gets into opponents' backfields on a consistent basis. He had 11.5 tackles for loss and five sacks in 2025, and while the sacks haven't really come yet in 2026, he's causing headaches for QBs with pressure. Echoles is explosive and can beat double-teams with his high effort level. He's also very effective in lateral pursuit. And I like his professional approach to the game.

19. KJ Duff, WR, Rutgers
Height: 6-6 | Weight: 225 | Previous rank: 17

2026 stats over eight games: 45 catches, 774 receiving yards, nine touchdown catches

You just aren't going to find wideouts with his skill set very often. Duff is a matchup nightmare at 6-foot-6, and offensive coordinators can line him up as a wideout, "move" tight end or even H-back because of that frame. Duff routinely uses his size to box out defenders. He attacks the ball in the air, and I see outstanding hands and body control. He adjusts well to off-target throws. Over his career, Duff has averaged 17.2 yards per catch, presenting his big-play potential.

Duff will miss the rest of the 2026 season, though, after undergoing high ankle surgery. He is expected to resume football activities in January.

20. Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State
Height: 6-4 | Weight: 205 | Previous rank: 19

2026 stats over 10 games: 36 tackles, seven pass breakups, 1.5 tackles for loss, 1 run stop

I had an eye on Jones last season for the 2026 class before he went back to school, and his consistency over these past two seasons is impressive. He anticipates well in coverage, and he uses his huge 6-foot-4 frame and long arms to attack receivers in press and make plays on the ball. Jones has only two interceptions (both last season), but he has broken up 18 passes since the start of 2025.

Jones can fly, too. He could put up a really good 40 time at the combine in March. He's comfortable with his back to the QB and is disruptive at the catch point. And he's a willing tackler in run defense.

21. Jackson Harris, WR, LSU
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 202 | Previous rank: NR

2026 stats over 10 games: 55 catches, 864 receiving yards, nine touchdown catches

Harris runs silky smooth routes and is deceptively quick. After two seasons and six total catches at Stanford in 2023 and 2024, Harris posted a solid 49-963-12 line at Hawaii in 2025. And after a slowish start to this season, his game has taken off over the past two months. I'm not sure there's another player in the class who has improved their stock since August as much as Harris. He makes tough grabs, can stretch the field (17.4 yards per catch over his career) and has plenty of after-the-catch ability.

22. Reed Harris, WR, Arizona State
Height: 6-5 | Weight: 220 | Previous rank: NR

2026 stats over 10 games: 59 catches, 987 receiving yards, nine touchdown catches

I really like Harris' length, physicality and sure hands. He has only four drops over 218 career targets, and he has 13 contested catches on the 2026 season. He's a big-play guy -- his career average is 18.5 yards per reception -- who tracks the ball well and wins consistently in tight coverage. Harris is a nightmare matchup for smaller cornerbacks. He was solid at Boston College over three seasons, but Arizona State has unlocked another level from him this year.

23. Dante Moore, QB, Oregon
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 220 | Previous rank: 23

2026 stats over four games: 69.7% completion rate, 926 passing yards, nine touchdown passes, zero interceptions; 22 rushing yards

Moore's season is likely over after taking a hit against USC and suffering a concussion. Scouts will want to see him healthy in the predraft process, but there will also be questions about whether Moore could return to school because he played only four games in 2026.

When Moore is at the top of his game, he's an impressive passer. He changes arm angles, he's mechanically sound, he displays precise ball placement, and there's good touch on his deep ball. Throws look effortless because of his arm strength, and he can deliver strikes while rolling out. There's even some scramble ability there. The toolbox is full.

But can he take over games against top-tier competition? His performance against Penn State in 2025 (at a time when the Nittany Lions were the No. 3 team in the country) was exceptional. I thought he was going to build on that and enter the 2026 draft as one of the top QBs on the board. But he couldn't bottle that performance and repeat it against other top teams over the rest of that 2025 season. And it doesn't seem like he will get the chance in 2026.

24. LaNorris Sellers, QB, South Carolina
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 238 | Previous rank: NR

2026 stats over nine games: 62.8% completion rate, 2,100 passing yards, 17 touchdown passes, seven interceptions; 718 rushing yards, seven rushing touchdowns

The traits are all there. Sellers has the size. He has the live arm. And he absolutely has the mobility, with his 6.1 yards per rush ranking third among FBS quarterbacks. But his inconsistent accuracy and decision-making will make for a challenging evaluation for NFL teams. The ball location can be erratic. But you can't teach his skill set, and I wouldn't be surprised if a general manager bets on the toolbox. Sellers has cut down his sacks (42 last year, just 18 so far this season), and he has plenty of experience with 33 career starts, despite being only 21 years old. He's just going to have to be in the right situation with the right coaching staff.

25. Arch Manning, QB, Texas
Height: 6-4 | Weight: 222 | Previous rank: 22

2026 stats over 10 games: 64.7% completion rate, 2,198 passing yards, 19 touchdown passes, 10 interceptions; 351 rushing yards, three rushing touchdowns

I see the size, mobility and arm strength that NFL teams look for in a franchise quarterback. He can make throws rolling out, and he is dangerous as a runner (10 rushing touchdowns last season).

But Manning is too inconsistent, especially when it comes to accuracy and decision-making. We saw that against LSU, with Manning throwing three interceptions and completing just 54.3% of his passes. He's going to be a tough evaluation. Watch just about any game he plays, and you'll ride the roller coaster of getting excited about his NFL ceiling and then wondering whether he's ever going to truly put it all together. Manning doesn't see the field as well as other quarterbacks on this list, and he occasionally throws off balance. And while the accuracy is better this season than it was in 2025, it still has to improve.

Position rankings
Quarterbacks
1. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State

2. CJ Carr, Notre Dame

3. Darian Mensah, Miami (Fla.)

4. Dante Moore, Oregon

5. LaNorris Sellers, South Carolina

Just missed: Arch Manning, Texas; Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss

Just missed: Isaac Brown, Louisville; Justice Haynes, Georgia Tech; Mark Fletcher Jr., Miami (Fla.)

Just missed: Reed Harris, Arizona State; Cam Coleman, Texas; Ryan Coleman-Williams, Alabama

1. Trey'Dez Green, LSU

2. Jamari Johnson, Oregon

Just missed: Patrick Overmyer, Houston; Willie Rodriguez; Kentucky; Andrew Rappleyea, Penn State

stories.headline: Mauricio Pochettino's 1st Man United training session filmed by drone operator
stories.summary: Video footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United head coach has appeared on YouTube after it was filmed by a drone operator.
stories.body:
Video footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United head coach has appeared on YouTube after it was filmed by a drone operator.

Around 12 minutes of the session was posted online on Thursday -- Pochettino's first full day in the job after arriving in Manchester on Wednesday. United have declined to comment.

- Pochettino: Man United players must relearn 'about being winners'

- Predicting the rest of the Premier League season: How all 20 teams will finish

- After a decade of near misses, Man United finally get their man in Pochettino

The footage shows Pochettino -- who signed a two-and-a-half year deal to take over from Michael Carrick last week -- working with a group of players while another two groups work separately under the supervision of his assistant, Jesus Perez.

Audio from the footage of United's Carrington training base could be heard, with the man appearing to operate the drone saying "let's get closer," before zooming in on Pochettino.

Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo were among the players shown working with Pochettinho.

"I can definitely see Harry Maguire," added the man providing commentary. "That there is Bruno [Fernandes], definitely, [I can] tell by the gestures."

Perez, along with staff members Toni Jimenez and Sebastiano Pochettino, arrived at Carrington earlier in the week after being released from their commitments with the USMNT ahead of Pochettino's final game in charge against Haiti on Tuesday.

The account justified the filming in a pinned post that said it's legal.

"It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone," the post said. "The drone is correctly labelled and I hold all the relevant licenses, public liability and insurance required."

The post said no sensitive information had been revealed with regard to how struggling United would line up at fourth-place Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

"As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager's first training session," wrote the poster. "There are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."

Pochettino travelled directly from Cincinnati to Manchester immediately after his final match with the USMNT and arrived at Carrington on Wednesday afternoon. His first game as United head coach is against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Sources: Spurs' Dylan Harper out 1-3 weeks with hip strain
stories.summary: Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday.
stories.body:
San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday.

This type of strain will carry a one-to-three-week timetable for return, dependent on Harper's rehab.

Harper was injured when he appeared to slip on a wet spot in the team's 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons in San Antonio on Tuesday night. Harper writhed on the floor in pain after the play and appeared to grab at his groin area.

Teammates Keldon Johnson and David Jones Garcia initially escorted Harper to the tunnel before the second-year guard put his arm over the shoulder of a staffer who helped him down the hallway.

Harper is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 15 games this season.

stories.headline: Messi leads way as MLS salaries rise; Union's Sullivan checks in at $614K
stories.summary: Inter Miami CF star Lionel Messi remains the highest-paid player in MLS, though the number of players making at least $10 million grew to five.
stories.body:
Inter Miami CF star Lionel Messi remains the highest-paid player in MLS, though the number of players making at least $10 million grew to five.

According to the MLS Players Association, Messi's guaranteed compensation remained $28.33 million, the same as during the spring salary release, though it is up from $20.45 million a year ago. Other players in the over $10 million club include the Chicago Fire FC's Robert Lewandowski ($19.51 million), Orlando City SC forward Antoine Griezmann ($13.94 million), LAFC's Son Heung-Min ($11.25 million) and Atlanta United FC forward Breel Embolo ($10.81 million).

All told, 150 of the league's players make at least $1 million in guaranteed compensation.

As in previous years, Messi's number reflects just the playing portion of his compensation. Last October, Messi signed a contract extension through the 2028 campaign. Inter Miami owner Jorge Mas told Bloomberg in March that Messi's total income is between $70 million to $80 million per year. Messi is also expected to acquire an equity stake in the club once he retires.

All data is as of Oct. 9, 2026. The salary data was annualized for players who arrived during the summer transfer window.

Miami continues to obliterate the competition in terms of total team spending. Thanks in part to the midseason arrival of midfielder Casemiro, Miami increased its spending to a record $59.37 million, though it finished second in the Eastern Conference behind Supporters Shield winners Nashville SC, which spent just $24.97 million. Miami's outlay is more than double the amount spent by 25 of the league's remaining 29 teams.

In terms of team payroll based on guaranteed base compensation, Chicago ranked second behind Miami at $41.29 million, due in part to the midseason arrival of Lewandowski. The Fire were followed by Atlanta United ($38.35 million), the LA Galaxy ($34.91 million) and LAFC ($32.91 million)

The Philadelphia Union had the league's lowest payroll at $12.64 million. Budding star Cavan Sullivan's guaranteed compensation checked in at a relatively modest $614,000. The next lowest payrolls after the Union were Sporting Kansas City ($13.30 million), D.C. United ($14.55 million), CF Montreal ($15.02 million) and FC Dallas ($15.49 million).

The average guaranteed base compensation for the entire MLS player pool -- which included pool players and retired players still owed money -- continues to climb on an annual basis, rising to $746,936, up 18% from the October 2025 mark of $632,809.

The salaries of players at the bottom of the wage scale continue to improve, though not at the same rate as those at the top. The league's median guaranteed base compensation was $360,042, up 6.4% from the October 2025 mark of $338,347.

MLS and the MLSPA are in the sixth year of the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) that was agreed upon in February 2021. The current CBA runs through the end of 2027.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen on F1 retirement, Le Mans and learning to lose: 'Stress a bit less'
stories.summary: Max Verstappen spoke to ESPN on his racing ambition and life beyond Formula 1.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen spent four years making winning in Formula 1 look almost routine. But after two seasons without a world championship, the Red Bull driver has found himself on the other side of a title fight -- and discovered that losing doesn't weigh quite as heavily as it once might have.

The Verstappen of 2021 was desperate for a world crown after five seasons at Red Bull in which he had proved his star quality but never quite had the car to match. The Verstappen of 2026? Even a difficult start to the season -- one that had him seriously questioning his future -- hasn't stopped him finding his way back to the front.

Now back second in the championship and showing the sort of form which is ominous for his 2027 rivals, Verstappen told ESPN that his perspective has changed and he "stresses a bit less" than he did when he was fighting for his first.

"Once you've won a lot, probably you can also put it into perspective a little bit better and you probably stress a little bit less about it," the Dutchman said ahead of the São Paulo Grand Prix.

"When I joined Formula 1 and then for a long time, we just never really had a chance to even fight closely for a title. You have the occasional race win. Then you go on to win, of course, a lot. And now, yeah, it's a little bit different."

Last year's title race went down to the wire, a nail-biting three-way battle between Verstappen and McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

Verstappen recovered from a 104-point deficit in August to trail Norris by just 12 points heading into the season finale in Abu Dhabi, with the British driver crowned the eventual champion.

At the start of the 2026 season, Red Bull struggled and dropped back from the front-runners, but a series of major upgrades helped Verstappen fight his way back into contention. He has since leapfrogged to second in the title standings behind new world champion Kimi Antonelli with three races to go.

Verstappen has claimed three victories this season, in Malaysia, Singapore and Mexico City.

"Last year, we were still very close to the title," Verstappen added. "This year, we had a bit of a rough start, but then actually, lately, we've been doing a really good job.

"We're actually winning races and second in the championship again at the moment."

- Max Verstappen: I don't need Kimi Antonelli to motivate me to stay in F1

- Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

How much longer will Verstappen stay in F1?

Verstappen raised the possibility of retiring at the end of 2026 after expressing frustration with F1's new regulations earlier this year, questioning whether he still enjoyed racing enough to justify the demands of the calendar.

But despite his criticism, the 29-year-old insists he remains fully committed to the sport.

"At the moment, it's just that I still love to do it," he told ESPN. "I still enjoy racing. I still love the competition.

"So it's probably more like if you wake up one day, you say like you can't commit 100% anymore. That's probably where you have to say to yourself, OK, it's maybe time for something else. But that's not at the moment."

Verstappen has been particularly critical of F1's new power-unit regulations, while also advocating for a return to simpler V8 engines. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has since hinted at the possibility of V8 engines returning in 2030.

Asked if the engine changes have impacted Verstappen's decision to stay in F1, he said: "I have a contract until 2030.

"And I think, first of all, we just want to go back to fighting for a title now in the coming years and then just see over time, you know, how everything is evolving.

"For sure, next year, it will change a little bit, probably a little bit for the better. And hopefully, of course, from next year onwards already, you know, we can be more in a title fight. That's definitely the goal as a team."

Le Mans, the Nurburgring and life beyond F1
Away from F1, Verstappen has been exploring side quests, one of them being racing at the iconic 24 hours race at the Nürburgring in May.

Verstappen was dreaming of victory on his debut, racing under his own team Verstappen Racing, which he founded in 2022. Despite leading the race, the car suffered a driveshaft issue with three hours remaining, forcing the team and Verstappen to retire.

He also competed in Portugal last month for the GT World Challenge after some of his team's drivers couldn't make the race due to a calendar clash. Verstappen stepped in and fought back his way through the field from 24th to ninth.

Asked if there was a race he could compete in tomorrow, he replied: "For me, that's either the racing in the Nordschleife, the 24 hours like I did already this year, or probably in Le Mans, in the hypercar class now."

But he did not give a timeframe on when he would compete in either event.

"Whenever I feel like I'm ready for it, or whenever it's the best chance to do it, I will do it," he added.

Verstappen Racing develops young drivers and has signed the likes of McLaren junior driver Dries van Langendonck. The 15-year-old Belgian currently competes in British Formula 4 and will be receiving guidance and simulator access through Verstappen's management company.

But Verstappen has ruled out taking on a role that would require him to travel the world running a top-level motorsport team.

He said: "Definitely not. Definitely not. No, no, no. I don't want to be travelling the world that many times a year. No, that's not for me."

Verstappen's word of advice for those youngsters trying to make a breakthrough is to always just be yourself, something Verstappen is known for up and down the grid.

"What I always want to tell them is you have to be yourself," he said.

"You can, of course, look at people and maybe pick up on some things or use that as maybe some guidance.

"But for me, it's very, very important that the driver always acts as themselves, not try to act like someone else. Because if you try to copy someone, you can only be just as good as them.

"And I feel like you really have to just rely on your own strengths and really take that to the next level."

- Lando Norris, Max Verstappen confident in F1's decision to race in Middle East

Which F1 races would Verstappen recommend to fans?
Verstappen's travels have also given him a unique perspective on the best races for fans to experience.

Speaking as a Heineken 0.0 ambassador ahead of the announcement of its 2027 F1 Season Ticket winner, who will receive flights, accommodation and tickets to every Grand Prix alongside a friend, Verstappen gave his insight into the race a fan should definitely not miss.

He said: "Honestly, the one that I think is really cool because, you know, the track is really nice to watch, but at the same time have a great time in the city as well.

"I think it's actually Budapest. I always think that people can have a really good time there. Yeah, just spending it with probably maybe friends even.

"You have a good time in the city, you then travel to the track and yeah, you have a cool experience at the track as well."

That winner has now been revealed as Lukáš Chalabala, a Czech F1 fan from Prague who has never attended a Grand Prix in person. Chalabala was selected through a fan vote after reaching the final six and was presented with his ticket at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where Verstappen joined the celebrations.

Verstappen believes attending every race as a fan would offer a deeper understanding of the sport.

He said: "Well, you probably get a lot more insights as well, right?

"When you get to go to every race, you probably understand a little bit more the details or the things that you're doing throughout practice, you know, to try and get the most out of a race weekend than maybe just visiting it once in a while or only once in your life or whatever. You never know."

Another race Verstappen singled out was Mexico City, where the atmosphere in the grandstands is particularly memorable.

"You do see if it's a crazy atmosphere, people are cheering," he added. "So, for example, I think one of the crazy ones, for sure, but in a good way crazy, is in Mexico, where they are, of course, very loud.

"They really cheer you on. They might cheer a little bit more for Checo [Sergio Pérez], but in general, yeah, it's a really nice race to visit and be part of the celebration in the stands and probably also see a little bit more of the culture of what Mexico is about."

stories.headline: Kayla Harrison, Amanda Nunes reclaim leading roles in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Who do Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes replace in ESPN's P4P women's top 10?
stories.body:
Hello (again), Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes. Goodbye (for now), Valentina Shevchenko and Zhang Weili. The top of the ESPN women's MMA pound-for-pound rankings has a new look.

Harrison and Nunes, both of whom had been ineligible for the top 10 because of inactivity, returned over the weekend for a clash of elites at UFC 334. Harrison, defending her bantamweight championship for the first time after nearly a year and a half out of the cage while healing from surgery for herniated discs in her neck, scored a fourth-round submission of Nunes, who had been retired for nearly 3½ years. As a result, Harrison takes over the No. 1 ranking and Nunes, a former two-division champion and the consensus GOAT of women's MMA, is No. 2.

The former occupants of those spots, Shevchenko and Zhang, are newly ineligible for the rankings because it's been over a year since they have fought and they have nothing scheduled. Those two former champions drop out, and the rest of the women's top 10 remains the same.

In the men's rankings, UFC heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane moves up one spot to No. 7 on the strength of his decision win over Josh Hokit in their title bout at UFC 334.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Nov. 18. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Kayla Harrison

UFC bantamweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 20-1

Last: W (Sub4) vs. Amanda Nunes, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Harrison stepped into the Octagon at UFC 334 already a reigning champion, but her submission win over Nunes was truly her crowning achievement. The backstory about their shared training gym history added drama to the buildup, but what mattered most about this matchup was that Harrison, who had voiced her goal to be the greatest ever in women's MMA, was facing the woman who has lived up to that standard. After choking out Nunes, what can Harrison do for an encore? Can any other woman in the sport give her a fight? Maybe it won't come to that. Harrison and Nunes both called for a rematch -- but at featherweight. That would lessen Harrison's burden in dealing with her toughest foe: the weigh-in scale.

2. Amanda Nunes

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 23-6

Last: L (Sub4) vs. Kayla Harrison, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Nunes' return from retirement did not go as she had hoped, but her failing was not so much about deteriorated physical abilities as it was about her ill-advised choice to venture too much into the grappling wheelhouse of Harrison, a two-time Olympic judo gold medalist. If Nunes gets the rematch both women are calling for, but this time at 145 pounds, that would seem to be to the advantage of Harrison, the bigger woman. But a redo would give Nunes another opportunity to lean into her own prodigious strength as a striker.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 13-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Virna Jandiroba, Nov. 7

Next: TBA

If Suarez was still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Loopy Godínez. Then she went on to beat another fellow top-10 strawweight, Jandiroba, sending a message to the division that Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

8. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

9. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

10. Jasmine Jasudavicius

UFC flyweight

Record: 16-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Erin Blanchfield, Oct. 17

Next: TBA

Jasudavicius was rising in the 125-pound division until being knocked out by Manon Fiorot last year, halting a five-fight winning streak. But she got back up and won two in a row, most recently an impressive grappling performance against Blanchfield, to reassert herself as a contender.

Other fighter receiving votes: Joselyne Edwards and Virna Jandiroba.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Kayla Harrison; 2. Amanda Nunes; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Tatiana Suarez; 6. Cris Cyborg; 7. Alexa Grasso; 8. Manon Fiorot; 9. Dakota Ditcheva; 10. Virna Jandiroba.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Nunes; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Jasmine Jasudavicius.

Andrew Davis: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Suarez; 10. Jasudavicius.

Dre Waters: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Nunes; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Joselyne Edwards.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Suarez; 9. Ditcheva; 10. Jasudavicius.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 29-4

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Movsar Evloev, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. He did just that by handing Evloev his first loss at UFC 333.

3. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 21-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career, then completing his trilogy with Dvalishvili with a successful title defense. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet.

4. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

5. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: Jan. 30 vs. Manel Kape

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

7. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 15-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Josh Hokit, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ made his first defense against Hokit at UFC 334, winning a slugfest.

8. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 7

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

9. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 21-6

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. Their third meeting at UFC 333 was the most competitive in their trilogy, but Dvalishvili fell short again.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: Dec. 12 vs. Sergei Pavlovich

Pereira made a big splash in the MMA after a world championship career in kickboxing. He joined the UFC in 2021 and became a middleweight champion the following year, then moved on to be a two-time light heavyweight titlist before making an unprecedented bid for a belt in a third weight class when he fought Game at UFC Freedom 250 for an interim heavyweight title. Pereira got knocked out in that fight, but now he's back on his feet and in position to reclaim his position when he faces a fellow title contender, Pavlovich, at UFC 335.

stories.headline: As Nike replaces Adidas, is UEFA Champions League star ball on its way out?
stories.summary: Nike will replace Adidas as supplier of UEFA Champions League match balls from next season. Will the famous 'star ball' design soon be no more?
stories.body:
Editor's note: This article was first published on Aug. 26, 2026 and has been updated

The UEFA Champions League and UEFA Women's Champions League match balls will boast a brand new look starting next season after UEFA confirmed on Monday that Nike will be taking over from long-standing provider Adidas as the official supplier for the 2027-28 campaign onwards.

Nike will take the reins for the 2027-28 campaign onward after agreeing a deal to supply the official match balls for all three UEFA club competitions from 2027 to 2031 -- the Champions League, the Europa League and the Conference League. According to The Guardian, that deal is worth around $45 million a year, double the value of the final contract with Adidas.

- Man United, Pochettino's to-do list based on what's gone wrong

- Meet Como's Paz, the heir to Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt

- Champions League talking points: Are Como the real deal?

With Adidas having supplied the official Champions League match ball since 2001, the "star ball" design has become an emblem of the competition. However, the last we see of the iconic pattern might be in the 2026-27 final.

That's because, as things stand, there are no specific details available as to the designs that Nike has in store. In a statement on Monday, UEFA would only say: "Further details on the match ball designs will be revealed in due course." It is also unclear -- and highly unlikely -- that the American sportswear giant will continue with the star theme popularised by Adidas over the past 25 years, as the German powerhouse reportedly hold the rights to the star ball design.

Nike's designs are therefore likely to be fresh and distinct with the intent of drawing a line under Adidas' tenure as UEFA match ball suppliers while also launching their own, modernised visual identity.

Back in August, Adidas unveiled what will be their final iteration of the "star ball," the preliminary eye-catching colourway of which is currently being used throughout the group phase of the 2026-27 Champions League.

The men's version of the 2026-27 Champions League ball is plastered in a neon-spattered livery that, according to Adidas, has been inspired by players creating colourful moments of magic and personal expression while plugging away at training on cold, foggy training pitches during their quest to attain Champions League greatness.

The design for the women's match ball is a little less abstract. The golden-orange pattern takes its inspiration from the aura of the ring of 11 stars that make up the UWCL emblem, with flashes of metallic purple and silver then adding a dash of visual contrast to the mix.

Both balls are based on the template that Adidas have used for their Champions League match balls since the introduction of the "Finale 1" ball for the 2001-02 season. Since then, over 50 iterations of the UCL star ball have been deployed in the competition -- and that's not including the various hi-vis yellow variants that have been used in winter months over the years.

stories.headline: 2027 WNBA mock draft: Tempo win lottery, projected to pick JuJu Watkins at No. 1
stories.summary: Toronto edged Houston and got the top pick in Sunday's draft lottery. The Comets will pick No. 2 and the Mystics No. 3.
stories.body:
In what could be the JuJu Watkins sweepstakes, the Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft. The Tempo won the draft lottery Sunday, with the Houston Comets picking second and the Washington Mystics third.

The Seattle Storm have the No. 4 pick, the Portland Fire got No. 5 and the Los Angeles Sparks have Nos. 6 and 7.

The Tempo, an expansion team in 2026, finished 11-33 last season, missing the playoffs. They were last in the league in defensive rating and won just one game after the All-Star break.

All of that could be much improved in 2027 with a player such as Watkins in Toronto. The national player of the year as a sophomore for the USC Trojans, Watkins missed last season after a knee injury suffered in the 2025 NCAA tournament. She has looked great so far this season and would fit in well with any WNBA team.

This is just Watkins' third college season, but age-wise, she is eligible for the draft. It is unknown if she will go pro or return to USC, but for now we are including her in the mock draft. If she decides Toronto is an unappealing destination or just wants to spend another season in college, she can wait until the 2028 draft.

That said, there is also uncertainty about the seniors who already have completed three seasons. Under the NCAA's new age-based eligibility model -- the five-seasons-in-five-years rule -- they could return for the 2027-28 season. So a lot about the draft pool remains speculative.

But now we know the lottery order.

1. Toronto Tempo: JuJu Watkins
USC | guard | 6-foot-2 | senior

Watkins and the Trojans are 3-1 after a close loss Sunday to No. 1 South Carolina in which she had 25 points. The March 2025 knee injury that forced Watkins to miss last season has not slowed her. She is averaging 24.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 3.3 steals. The Tempo's strength last season was at guard, led by Marina Mabrey. If Watkins doesn't declare for the draft, there should still be good players available for the Tempo. But perhaps not an immediate franchise-changer as Watkins is expected to be.

2. Houston Comets: Madison Booker
Texas | forward | 6-foot-1 | senior

Like several teams, Texas has not been tested yet. But Booker has displayed why she's a lottery pick in the three games she has played so far, including a 30-point, six-assist game against Northern Colorado. Booker's size, strength and confidence on offense and her versatility on defense should translate to the pro game. She took a hard fall in Wednesday's win over South Dakota State and did not play in Sunday's victory against Tarleton State, but she is not expected to miss much more time. The Comets -- the Connecticut Sun relocated as a revived franchise -- last played in the 2008 WNBA season. The Sun were tied for next to last with Toronto at 11-33 this year, and it's fair to say they could use help in all areas, which would make Booker appealing.

3. Washington Mystics: Hannah Hidalgo
Notre Dame | guard | 5-foot-6 | senior

Hidalgo has carried a heavy load throughout her college career, and that continues her senior season. In four victories, she has averaged 28.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.8 steals while shooting 59.4% from the field. Hidalgo is a huge threat on offense and defense and could really add to the young core already there if she goes to the Mystics. Washington could use more 3-point shooting. While Hidalgo wasn't great from beyond the arc last season (36 of 142, 25.4%), she shot 40% from 3-point range as a sophomore and is at 40% so far this season.

4. Seattle Storm: Tessa Johnson
South Carolina | guard | 6-foot-1 | senior

Johnson's 3-point shooting is an impressive tool that will translate to the pro game. She was the top power-conference player in the country last season in 3-point percentage (44.8%, 90 of 201). So far this season, she is 9-for-18 (50%) from beyond the arc and is averaging 17.0 points. She had 28 points in Sunday's victory over USC. The Storm were last in the WNBA this past season at 8-36 and could benefit from another dynamic young guard to go along with the young post talent they have.

5. Portland Fire: Mikaylah Williams
LSU | guard | 6-foot | senior

The Tigers have cruised through four blowouts, and Williams' averages -- 19.0 points, 5.3 rebounds and 5.5 assists while shooting 58% from the field and 45.5% from beyond the arc -- don't tell us anything we didn't expect. She's a pro-ready player on the offensive end who can look to improve defensively in the WNBA. The expansion Fire had a solid season in 2025, going 17-27, and Williams could fit in offensively.

6. Los Angeles Sparks: Kymora Johnson
Virginia | guard | 5-foot-7 | senior

The Cavaliers are 5-0, and we will know more about them once they play their tougher nonconference foes, such as Oklahoma on Nov. 23. But so far, Johnson has looked very good, averaging 18.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 2.2 steals while shooting 59.6% from the field and 61.3% from beyond the arc (13 of 21). With back-to-back picks, Los Angeles can address two of several needs with this draft. The Sparks were 16-28 this season and missed the playoffs for the sixth year in a row.

7. Los Angeles Sparks: Sarah Cissé
France | forward | 6-foot-2

There's so much we don't know now about the Sparks -- including who their coach will be for 2027 -- as they move on after future Hall of Famer Nneka Ogwumike's retirement. But Cissé is another talented player out of France who could make an impact on the WNBA. The MVP of the U20 European Championships this summer, she turns 20 in January. The Sparks were next to last in the WNBA in rebounding this past season, so Cissé might be able to help there.

8. New York Liberty: Ainhoa Risacher
France | forward | 6-foot-1

If you recognize the last name, Risacher is the younger sister of Zaccharie Risacher, the NBA's No. 1 draft pick in 2024. A good-sized wing player, Risacher competed alongside Cissé on France's winning U20 European Championships team this past summer. She will turn 20 in July. The Liberty had an up-and-down 2026 season, getting the No. 8 seed in the playoffs. They knocked off No. 1 Minnesota but then were swept by No. 4 Atlanta. New York fired Chris DeMarco after just one season, so we await their next coach. The Liberty already have a strong French/international presence. The question might be if Risacher impresses them enough defensively compared with other draft options.

9. Dallas Wings: Chloe Kitts
South Carolina | forward | 6-foot-2 | senior

Kitts missed last season because of a knee injury but has looked great so far. A starter as a junior, she averaged 10.2 points and 7.7 rebounds in 2024-25. Through four games this season, she has three double-doubles and is averaging 13.0 points and 10.0 rebounds. In Sunday's victory over USC, Kitts had 15 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and four steals. If she continues to play this well, we could see her move up the draft board. Still, with Dallas having young guards such as Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd, Kitts could be a good addition for the Wings, who made the playoffs at 27-17 this season.

10. Indiana Fever: Talaysia Cooper
Ole Miss | guard | 6-foot-0 | senior

The Fever are facing two huge offseason questions: Will free agent guard Kelsey Mitchell return, and who will be their general manager? Indiana could use help at the wing position with a player who can defend at a high level but also score. That could be Cooper, who is playing for her third SEC program and averaging 14.0 points while shooting 37% (10 of 27) from 3-point range. She showed progress from beyond the arc last season, and if that continues this season it will help her draft prospects. Cooper had her best defensive season as a sophomore at Tennessee, and a return to that level will boost her.

11. Chicago Sky: Khamil Pierre
NC State | forward | 6-foot-2 | senior

Pierre doesn't shoot the 3 much, but she is relentless in the paint. After two strong years at Vanderbilt, she transferred to NC State and led the ACC in rebounding last season (11.9 RPG) while averaging 16.7 points and shooting 52.5% from the field. So far this season for the 4-1 Wolfpack, she is averaging 21.2 points and 8.4 rebounds while shooting 51.3%. The injury-plagued Sky went 16-28 and missed the playoffs for the third year in a row this past season. They were 13th in offensive rating and 10th in rebounding, and Pierre might help in both areas.

12. Chicago Sky: S'Mya Nichols
Kansas | guard | 6-foot | senior

Nichols is off to a little slower start than expected, averaging 12.5 points and 4.3 assists. (She averaged 17.4 and 4.6 last season.) That's why she has fallen from No. 6 in our two previous mock drafts. But to be fair, it's still early in the season. Nichols had 12 points and six assists in the Jayhawks' loss to Nebraska on Saturday. She and Kansas have another shot at a ranked team this week at Minnesota on Wednesday.

13. Dallas Wings: Kaylene Smikle
Tennessee | guard | 6-foot-0 | senior

Smikle started her career at Rutgers, then went to Maryland and is now at Tennessee. She played just seven games last year with the Terps, missing the rest of the season after knee surgery. So far this season, she is leading the 4-0 Lady Vols with 22.3 points per game, while also averaging 6.0 rebounds. She is also off to a hot start from beyond the arc at 50% (12 of 24). Smikle could add guard/wing depth for Dallas.

14. Golden State Valkyries: Oluchi Okananwa
Maryland | guard | 5-foot-10 | senior

Okananwa is averaging 14.0 points and 6.3 rebounds, but the Terps have played just three games. She was first-team All-Big Ten and all-defense last season -- we know the WNBA champion Valkyries love defense -- but she probably will need to show improvement as a 3-point shooter to ensure being a first-round pick. So far this season she is 3-for-6 from beyond the arc.

15. Minnesota Lynx: Clara Strack
Kentucky | center | 6-foot-5 | senior

Sunday was another big stats day for Strack, who had 29 points and 18 rebounds in a victory over Eastern Michigan. That included going 4-of-5 from beyond the arc, which is important: It's not easy for traditional centers to find their way in the WNBA, so having shooting range matters. Strack has shown that, making 42 3-pointers over the past two seasons. She is 8-of-21 from 3-point range so far this season. Strack, who was the SEC's defensive player of the year in 2025, is averaging 18.4 points, 9.6 rebounds and 3.8 blocks for the 5-0 Wildcats.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.
